scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You tap a tiny button on your screen, and it knows exactly where. But glass can't feel. So how?

scenes.name: grid
scenes.text: Under the glass is an invisible grid of transparent wires. Rows one way, columns the other.

scenes.name: field
scenes.text: The phone sends a tiny signal through each row, and every crossing point holds a small electric field, called capacitance.

scenes.name: finger
scenes.text: Your finger conducts electricity. Near a crossing, it pulls away some of that field, so the measured value drops.

scenes.name: scan
scenes.text: A controller chip checks every crossing, over a hundred times a second, looking for those drops.

scenes.name: center
scenes.text: Your finger covers several crossings. It weighs how much each one dropped, and finds the exact centre, finer than the grid.

scenes.name: multi
scenes.text: Since every crossing is measured separately, it tracks many fingers at once. And a normal glove doesn't conduct, so it fails.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Grid, field, finger, centre. Glass that feels you. Follow for more on how things really work.
